item.research_question: How does ambient temperature influence the wear resistance, lattice structure, dislocation evolution, friction coefficient, hardness, and elastic modulus of FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coatings on a Cu matrix?
item.material_system: FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating (21 Å thick) on a single crystal Cu matrix (FCC lattice, 3.56 Å constant)
item.processing_route: Molecular dynamics simulation using LAMMPS; model relaxed via conjugate gradient and Nosé–Hoover thermostat (NPT/NVT ensembles); temperatures set at 300 K, 600 K, 900 K, and 1200 K; friction simulation at 10 m/s speed with 10 Å depth; nanoindentation at 10 m/s speed with 30 Å depth over 300 ps loading/unloading
item.test_conditions: Temperatures: 300 K, 600 K, 900 K, 1200 K; Friction speed: 10 m/s; Indentation speed: 10 m/s; Indenter radius and force constant K = 3 eV/Å; Periodic boundary conditions in X and Y; Fixed boundary in Z
key_findings: With increasing temperature, the friction coefficient gradually increased, especially from 900 K to 1200 K where fluctuation intensified.
At 300 K and 600 K, the hardness of the coating was basically the same, but at 900 K it dropped from 17.4 GPa to 10.2 GPa, and at 1200 K it further decreased to 8.6 GPa.
The elastic modulus increased from 173 GPa at 300 K to 219 GPa at 600 K, then declined rapidly at 900 K and 1200 K.
At 600 K, the dislocation density was significantly reduced compared to 300 K, which the authors attribute to the increase in elastic modulus.
At 900 K and 1200 K, dislocation density increased rapidly, leading to a significant decrease in both hardness and elastic modulus.
The normal force decreased significantly with temperature due to thermal softening, dropping by about 20 nN from 300 K to 900 K and by about 40 nN at 1200 K.
At 1200 K, the Cu matrix began to melt with a large number of disordered structures appearing, while the high entropy alloy coating remained mostly FCC.
The wear degree of the coating obviously increased with temperature, with the wear resistance decreasing sharply when the temperature reached 900 K.
item.mechanism: The authors argue that increasing temperature leads to greater lattice disorder and changes in dislocation density. Specifically, the reduction in dislocation density at 600 K increases the elastic modulus, while the rapid increase in dislocation density and atomic disorder at 900 K and 1200 K causes thermal softening, reduced hardness, and a sharp decline in wear resistance. The friction coefficient increase at high temperatures is attributed to the high proportion of disordered atoms and the stability of the tangential force despite the drop in normal force.
item.limitations: The authors state they did not analyze the effect of changes in the proportion of elements in the FeNiCrCoCu alloy on wear resistance, nor did they study the roughness of the material surface.
item.future_work: The authors propose conducting subsequent analysis by changing the proportion of elements to obtain the external influencing mechanism and studying the influence of surface roughness on wear resistance by changing the surface morphology of the material.
quotes: The density of dislocations at 600 K is significantly reduced compared with that at 300 K, resulting in an increase of the elastic modulus of the material from 173 GPa to 219 GPa.

At temperatures of 900 K and 1200 K, lattice disorder takes place rapidly, and dislocation density also decreases significantly, resulting in a significant decrease in the hardness and elastic modulus of the material.
When the temperature reaches 900 K, the wear resistance of the FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating decreases sharply.
